clue.text: Gallon of tea

parts.note: cong. is the abbreviation for congius, the Latin gallon used in old prescriptions
o' is the clipped form of of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: A huge quantity of tea, a whole gallon of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Mephisto relies on Chambers, which lists CONG as an abbreviation for congius, a gallon.
explanation.definitionFit: Congo, also spelt congou, is a kind of black China tea listed in Chambers.

clue.text: We benefit from trust in being protected by mitre

definitions.note: a clause standing for a plural noun: those who benefit from a trust

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed by it, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: in Chambers mitre can mean a girdle, and a cestus is a girdle
I is the self, a being

explanation.surface: A bishop's mitre seems to keep a trust's beneficiaries safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The mitre here is not a bishop's hat but an old word for a girdle, as worn in Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cestui que trust is the legal beneficiary of a trust, the plural being cestuis.

clue.text: Refusing to face facts in resort I risk hotel adding $100

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, so the letters are reordered
adding means one more piece is joined on to the others

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in denial about the bill at a resort hotel that adds a hundred dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostriches are said to bury their heads in the sand, an image of refusing to face reality.

clue.text: Sculptured character is reassuringly phat (in part)

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A carved figure is comfortingly cool, as slang has it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glyph is a carved figure or symbol, such as an ornamental groove or a hieroglyph cut in stone.

clue.text: This pitches high — way too magniloquent about plonk

parts.note: OTT is over the top, excessive
a is an abbreviation for about
plonk is cheap wine, vino

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off in an overblown way about cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottavino is the piccolo, an instrument whose notes sound an octave above the flute.

clue.text: Hounds wound up starter

indicators.note: something wound up is twisted round, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Racing dogs get excited by the man who starts the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratters are dogs kept for catching rats, so the word is a fair synonym for hounds.

clue.text: Rope with noose is up, voice curt term of gratitude

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to air a view is to voice it
ta is a short informal thank you

explanation.surface: A rope with a noose is ready and someone gives brief thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a lariat, a long rope with a running noose used for lassoing.

clue.text: Before noon draw a flask

parts.note: a.m. is ante meridiem, before noon
to draw is to pull
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a flask in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampulla is a small two-handled Roman bottle or flask for oil or perfume.

clue.text: Knitted tea cosy? Possibly this Mexican wrap, yes

indicators.note: knitted means woven together, so the letters are combined in a new order
the word at the end is what must be added to the answer, so taking it away leaves the answer

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woolly tea cosy is jokingly likened to a Mexican wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus yes, knitted together, make tea cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a folded Mexican tortilla wrapped around a filling.

clue.text: Conceal in shell nut near spinning in hull?

parts.note: an en, or nut, is a printer's measure

indicators.note: in places the turned piece within the next word

parts.note: the keel is the backbone of a ship's hull

indicators.note: spinning means turning round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: nr is the abbreviation for near

explanation.surface: A nut spinning inside its hull asks to be kept in the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: To enkernel is to enclose within a kernel or husk, hiding something in its shell.

clue.text: Wash in southern river

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the Ouse is one of several English rivers of that name

explanation.surface: Bathing in a river in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse is to drench or plunge in liquid, so it can mean wash.

clue.text: Old quack? Wit I am to proscribe cobalt

parts.note: salt is pungent wit, as in Attic salt
I am contracts to I'm
to proscribe is to forbid
Co is the chemical symbol for cobalt

explanation.surface: An old wit declares that cobalt must be banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltimbanco was an old word for a mountebank, a travelling seller of fake remedies, which is a quack.

clue.text: Rich judge accommodates press for charity event

parts.note: rich can mean highly amusing

indicators.note: accommodates means houses, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a game
Chambers gives lie as to weigh or press on something

explanation.surface: A wealthy judge lends a printing press for a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Comic Relief is a British charity whose telethon, Red Nose Day, is a well-known fundraising event.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic Relief runs Red Nose Day, a televised British fundraising occasion for good causes.

clue.text: Lace drink guy pushed forward

indicators.note: pushed forward tells us the guy's word goes to the front instead of following the drink

parts.note: a guy is a supporting rope, as is a stay on a ship
tape is old slang for liquor

explanation.surface: Someone spikes a drink and a man is shoved ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the pieces in the wrong order; the guy's word is moved in front of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay tape is a narrow binding braid sewn along edges of garments, a kind of lace or trimming.

clue.text: Hidden danger behind changing ends

indicators.note: changing ends asks for the first and last letters of the word to swap places

parts.note: prat is slang for the buttocks

explanation.surface: A lurking danger behind someone who keeps switching sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a concealed device or pitfall, a hazard that is out of sight.

clue.text: Such as you may get in manuscript headed by Edgar?

definitions.text: Such as you may get in manuscript headed by Edgar

indicators.note: headed by puts the poet's name at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
MS is the standard abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: What you would find in a handwritten draft with Edgar Allan Poe's name at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a Poe manuscript would hold verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe wrote famous verse such as The Raven, so his manuscripts would contain lyric compositions.

clue.text: Dandy lashes purple passages?

parts.note: a beau is a dandy, a fop
to lash is to tie down

explanation.surface: A fop whips florid writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple passages are showy fine writing, the kind of choice extracts once collected as beauties.

clue.text: Virginia left with prayer for stiff escort?

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
L is the usual abbreviation for left
the Kyrie eleison is a prayer in the Mass

explanation.surface: A woman from Virginia is left saying a prayer for a formal, stiff companion.
explanation.walkthrough: A stiff is slang for a corpse, not a formal person.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the Valkyries carried slain warriors to Valhalla, so they escort the dead.

clue.text: Mom looks up movement of commies

indicators.note: up here means stirred up or in disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother researches the history of a communist organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Komsomol was the Soviet Communist youth league, a political organisation of young communists.

clue.text: Picking up sledge at last I relax here

definitions.text: Picking up sledge at last I relax here

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: picking up means collecting something, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: to chill is to relax

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the last letter of sledge

explanation.surface: A tobogganer, having collected the sledge, unwinds at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: a slope of ice is where you would sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice hill is a frozen slope built or used for tobogganing, the spot where one sledges.

clue.text: String up over every other bit of gent's boundary marker?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: to string up is to hang, to lynch

indicators.note: every other bit means taking alternate letters

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Hanging a gentleman over the boundary line.
explanation.definitionFit: A lynchet is a cultivation terrace or unploughed bank between fields, which marks a boundary.

clue.text: Jaguar's boast brushing book aside

indicators.note: brushing something away sweeps it off, so a letter is dropped
aside completes brushing: the letter is set out of the way

parts.note: bounce is boastful swagger or bluster
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A jaguar boasts, sweeping a book out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounce names various wild cats, the snow leopard chiefly, and Chambers also allows the jaguar.

clue.text: Especially down about rising matadors

parts.note: esp. is the abbreviation for especially

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, the letters backwards

parts.note: down means sad
a is an abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Bullfighters, depressed above all, are on the up.
explanation.definitionFit: Espada is Spanish for sword, and in English it names the matador who wields one.

clue.text: What Scots farmers avoid is coarse linen

parts.note: is contracts to 's
harn is a coarse linen fabric

explanation.surface: Scottish farmers steer clear of rough linen cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmers avoid stepping in it: the word is Scots for cow dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharn is a Scots word for cattle dung, which a farmer would rather not tread in.

clue.text: Howls English held back in ages entering French gents

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is put within another
held back means taken out of its usual place and kept until later

parts.note: ages and years both mean a long time
E is the abbreviation for English
MM is the abbreviation for messieurs

explanation.surface: An Englishman waits for ages while French gentlemen come in.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of the ages word is held back so that it follows the French gents inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to wail or complain loudly, so yammers works as howls.

clue.text: Place (classy) with sound units for some concertgoers

parts.note: Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for Place
U means upper-class
a sone is a unit of loudness

explanation.surface: A posh venue with good acoustics for concert audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus-ones are invited guests' companions, so some people at a concert attend as someone's guest.

clue.text: What's on Dark Side of the Moon is in place of old concert

definitions.text: What's on Dark Side of the Moon

indicators.note: in place of means swapping one item out for another

parts.note: a Prom is a promenade concert
O is an abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about Pink Floyd's album and an old concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Pink Floyd's album The Dark Side of the Moon has a famous cover showing light split by a triangular glass shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The album cover pictures a prism splitting a beam of white light into a spectrum.

clue.text: Ham is withdrawn after being tipped

indicators.note: tipped means its tip, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: remote means aloof, withdrawn

explanation.surface: A bad actor goes quiet after being given a tip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to overact, and to emote is to show emotion theatrically.

clue.text: Eclectic Persian arts grad Auntie cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
Auntie and the Beeb are both nicknames for the BBC

explanation.surface: A Persian arts graduate with wide tastes, whose aunt is abrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: A Babee or Babi is a follower of the Bab, founder of an eclectic nineteenth-century Persian sect.

clue.text: Icons ducking special procedures

indicators.note: ducking means dodging, so the following abbreviation is left out

parts.note: sprites are small graphic images on a computer screen, like icons
SP is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Religious images avoiding special ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are formal ceremonial procedures, for example in church services.

clue.text: Foil for riposte? It's between sublime and peerless

indicators.note: and joins the end of one word to the start of the next
between points to the letters where the two words meet, the end of one and the start of the other

parts.note: the final letter
only its opening letters are kept, those nearest the word before

explanation.surface: An unmatched fencer's counterattack.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the junction of sublime and peerless.
explanation.definitionFit: The épée is a fencing sword, an alternative to the foil, used to riposte.

clue.text: Apostle quietly leaving a Roman hall

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes

parts.note: Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles
p is piano, quietly in music
taken as written

explanation.surface: An apostle tiptoes out of a Roman hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Aula is Latin for hall or court, used for a hall in a Roman house or palace.

clue.text: Tramp collecting money in dump finds diamond

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to dump something is to get rid of it

indicators.note: in places the whole first group inside the following word

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A tramp picking through a rubbish dump comes across a diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomboid is a parallelogram shape, the diamond outline of a rhombus with unequal sides.

clue.text: Speak the same lingo as throne and aim to brood no more

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat or throne
to eye is to aim at or look towards
taken as written
eye is an obsolete word for a brood of pheasants

explanation.surface: A monarch aiming to stop sulking talks like everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: No more marks the brood sense as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is to agree completely, which is speaking the same language in the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Silent about embedded doughboy's kitbag

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: mute means silent
set in concrete is embedded

explanation.surface: A soldier's bag lies silent with something stuck in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A doughboy is an American infantryman of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette bag is a small canvas shoulder bag issued to US soldiers, their kitbag.

clue.text: Ludicrous false thumbs

indicators.note: ludicrous means absurd or crazy, so the word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Absurd fake digits.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaf through a book is to thumb through it, flicking the pages.
